Nunn silty clay loam, 4 to 8 percent slopes (No).
This sloping soil is in 5 to 25 acre areas on fans and footslopes in intermittent stream valleys. Slopes are 4 to 5 percent on the fans and 7 to 8 percent on the footslopes immediately below the residual soils that border the valleys. The soil profile is similar to the typical one described for the series. Included with this soil in mapping are areas of Midway silty clay loam on isolated knolls or low ridges.
The surface runoff is medium, and the erosion hazard is moderate. Most areas on footslopes receive runoff from soils above them.
This soil is suited to dryland crops and range. It is also suited to irrigated crops.
(Capability Unit IIIe-2; IIIe-1 Irrigated; Clayey range site 10-14 inch precipitation zone; Windbreak Suitability Group 1).
Nunn-Midway silty clay loams, 4 to 15 percent slopes (NS).
This complex comprises sloping and moderately steep soils of the sedimentary plains. The complex consists of about 55 percent Nunn silty clay loam and about 25 percent Midway silty clay loam. Minor soils making up 20 percent are Thedalund loam and Wages loam. The Nunn silty clay loam is on the fans, footslopes, and valley bottom. Slopes are 4 to 10 percent and length is 50 to 200 feet. The Midway silty clay loam is on the knolls and ridges. Slopes are 10 to 15 percent. The Nunn and Midway soils in this complex have profiles similar to those described as typical for their respective series. Included with these soils in mapping are spots of Thedalund loam around sandstone outcrops. Spots of Wibaux channery loam are included in the valleys draining burned shale hills.
The surface runoff is medium, and the erosion hazard is moderate. Most areas receive runoff from soils that border the valleys.
This complex is suited to range. The Nunn soil is suited to limited cropland. Erosion control is important in managing the cultivated soil.
(Capability Unit IVe-3; Clayey range site 10-14 inch precipitation zone; Windbreak Suitability Group 1).
